policy_title: Scrutinise Royal Mail Takeover Bids and Explore New Governance Models
stated: Labour will ensure any proposed takeover of Royal Mail is robustly scrutinised, with appropriate guarantees to protect the interests of the workforce, customers, and the UK, including maintaining the universal service obligation. The party will also explore new business and governance models to give workers and customers a stronger voice in the company's direction.

source.quote: Royal Mail remains a key part of the UK’s infrastructure. Labour will ensure that any proposed takeover is robustly scrutinised and that appropriate guarantees are forthcoming that protect the interests of the workforce, customers and the United Kingdom, including the need to maintain a comprehensive universal service obligation. Labour will also explore new business and governance models for Royal Mail so that workers and customers who rely on Royal Mail services can have a stronger voice in the governance and strategic direction of the company.

bearing_set.reason: The policy explicitly targets workforce protections and worker voice in governance during any takeover, directly bearing on job security, employment conditions, and labour rights for Royal Mail employees.

Scrutinising foreign takeover bids of Royal Mail — critical national infrastructure holding extensive address and physical delivery data — directly bears on national security posture and resilience to external threats.

Protecting the Universal Service Obligation through takeover scrutiny preserves nationwide postal connectivity, which underpins economic participation and opportunity especially in rural and remote areas where commercial alternatives are absent.

membership_note: Three fundamentals each with a concrete mechanism: O4 (worker protections and voice), O5 (national security scrutiny of critical infrastructure), and O13 (USO as economic connectivity). The 'explore' language on governance models is tentative but the USO and workforce commitments are substantive enough to clear the non-negligible bar on all three.
